corrected_answer:

Diagnose by correlating request IDs and lifecycle timestamps with prompt/output tokens, live tokens, per-request KV bytes and growth, active/cancelled sequences, allocated/reserved bytes, largest free block, fragmentation, workspaces, collective buffers, cache retention, cleanup latency, and host RSS. Prioritize token/batch overcommit, then fragmentation or delayed frees, prefix-cache retention, transient workspaces, leaks, and host pressure.

Run warmed randomized baseline versus only a token-aware admission cap, repeated by strata with model/runtime/hardware fixed and confidence intervals; then isolate context/batch limits, paged KV, prefix caching, KV quantization, and allocator changes one at a time. Report completions, OOMs, explicit rejections, peak bytes/GiB, throughput, TTFT, TPOT, P99, correctness, and quality with separate denominators. Confounders include warm-up, asynchronous reclamation, workload drift, workspace selection, collectives, thermal throttling, and background use.

Mitigate with token-aware admission/backpressure, reserved headroom, bounded context/output and queue, and cancellation cleanup. Canary optimizations only with quality/latency gates; roll back on OOM/error, quality, SLO, or unsafe rejection regression.
